Contemporary World History – Hist 1103 Spring 2026-- Online Instructor: Dr. Bruce R. Homann Office: H229 Phone: 763-433-1129 x 1129 (from campus) I am not generally on campus during the summer, but feel free to use my Google Voice number. Google Voice phone #: 763-250-1129 (If I don’t answer, please call back from the same phone number in 5 minutes or “page” me in D2L Brightspace. Contact the help desk if you have any trouble with D2L Brightspace.) I won't answer a number I don't recognize, hence the reason for calling back in 5 minutes. You may also text my google voice number. Please identify yourself when you text and be patient for my reply. NOTE: This class is a 16 week course smashed into 4 weeks. Needless to say, we will be moving extremely fast through the course. The workload will also be very high. If you are unable to meet the deadlines or keep up with the workload, you should not take this class. There will be no special arrangements for vacations or altered turn-in dates due to work schedules. READ THIS SYLLABUS CAREFULLY and page me with any questions. Please also note that all students are expected to have access to the internet, know how to operate their computers, and be prepared to call the ARCC technical help desk for issues with D2L. Please check the ARCC website for any other help needed with navigating D2L. I will be holding “online” office hours as well as accepting appointments via Zoom. Generally, I will be online sporadically throughout the day to get messages and answer questions. Students may page me or email me. I can also arrange to be online for chatting (Zoom) ... if anyone would like to make an online “appointment” to chat with me, just let me know! Students may also reach me through “paging” me during online office hours through the D2L messaging App in the upper right corner (envelope Icon) Email: Bruce.Homann@anokaramsey.edu Office Hrs : Tues and Thurs 2-4 pm online (zoom), and by appointment. Course Description: This course will provide a survey of contemporary world history post WWII. We will discuss major historical events, processes and transformations and how they have shaped the modern world. Some of the topics included may be the Cold War, Korean War, Vietnam Conflict, Eastern European Uprisings, Communist China, Cuban Missile Crisis and Bay of Pigs, Middle

# Page 2^page=2
East (Israel & the PLO and Iran/Iraq), and South Asia (India & Pakistan), Africa, Latin America, international terrorism and the New World Order. Course Text: Contemporary World History Since 1945 by Jeffrey W. Jones. Published by Routledge, 2025. Course Goals: 1. To Think! 2. To learn the historical process and its application throughout world history 3. To learn and be able to discuss world issues, and how they affect the development of history. Exams and Exam Policy: There will be a Midterm exam that will take the form of position papers 1250 (minimum) to 3000+ words in length, and a Final that will be comprehensive and 1750 to 3000+ words in length. (There are approximately 250 words per typed page.) Due Thursdays at 11:30pm of the week on the schedule. Failure to meet word minimums will result in an “F” on each exam that falls short. Only the word count of the answer to the exam questions may apply to the word count minimums. Additionally, bibliographies are required, but do not count toward the word count total. Lastly, be sure your Turnitin score is 15% or less. This examines your similarity to other sources. If I ask to meet with you about your exam or assignments, your grade will be delayed until we meet and discuss the work submitted. Meetings must occur within one week of grades being returned to receive a passing grade. The questions for each exam will be posted by the instructor on Monday of the exam week by noon. Each exam will be due by 11:30pm on Thursday of the same week. The Midterm is due June 18th (Thursday) by 11:30 pm. The Final Exam is due July 2nd, Thursday, at 11:30pm. There is no provision for make up exams or other completion times without prior discussion and approval of the instructor. You must take both exams to pass this course. 80% of your grade. [Section exams = 30% each: Final = 50%.] The final will be essay and comprehensive. For every assignment or exams, I may want to follow up with you about your work (i.e., ask you questions) in real time via a zoom-meeting. Should I notify you of this intent, I will work with you to arrange a zoom or in-person meeting to discuss the submission. You should be prepared to discuss in detail your study and research and writing processes as you worked on the submission. Late exams: Any exams that arrive .1 (meaning past 11:31pm to 24 hours late = 1 day late: 24.1 to 48 hours late = 2 days late etc etc etc…. No Exceptions unless previously arranged with the instructor. Grades will be reduced by one full letter grade for every day late the exam is. Also, if the exam

# Page 3^page=3
submitted is in an unacceptable format, it will be counted as not having been submitted, so please be sure you submit work ONLY in the acceptable format listed in this syllabus. Please Note: When you are writing your exams and assignments, be sure to use your own words; don’t just rearrange words from your sources without citing them. That is plagiarism and will be handled in the manner already outlined in this syllabus. No more than 15% of your writing should come from another source (i.e. quotes or paraphrasing). This will be checked by TURNITIN. You can always ask me for individual feedback, or for help on determining what you should and shouldn’t cite. When in doubt, ASK! I am here to help. Assignments and Participation: 20% of your grade Each student is expected to read the material assigned and be prepared to discuss it by way of the message board. Assignments must be a minimum length of 400 words to receive credit. (I will count words—if you feel you do not need to obey this requirement, do NOT take this class.) They will be posted weekly and must be turned in by the due date. There will be 13 Assignments. Assignments for the week (usually 4) will be posted Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday by noon each day, and are due by Saturday at 11:30pm. There will be one assignment posted after the Midterm during the week the Midterm is assigned. Note: I may post the assignments early. This will not alter the due dates. They will be graded on a pass/fail basis. You will not receive a letter grade from me for assignments. Each student may easily track if they passed the assignment by following the criteria below. If anyone would like individual feedback on their assignment, please page me with your request and I will be happy to give you detailed feedback. Your criteria for acceptable assignments are as follows: 1.) minimum word length (400 words—feel free to go quite a bit over—this is a minimum, not a target) 2.) work turned in on time (late work = no points) to the Assignment tab dropbox AND Discussion section post. Assignments are to be posted as responses to my posted assignments in the Discussion section under the Discussions tab. Additionally, be sure to upload the file to the correct dropbox in the Assignments section under the Assignments tab. Please remember, only post in the Discussion section (do NOT use attachments when you post your assignment to the Discussion section.) and upload the file for the Assignment Dropbox. Both locations are required. 3.) Good faith effort at the assignment. (If you have to ask if you put forth a good faith effort, you probably did not.) This includes the use of good grammar and the citation of source material. Always cite your sources! (See link for CMOS – Chicago manual of style) https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/chicago_manual_17th_edition/cmos_formattin g_and_style_guide/general_format.html 4.) At the end of your assignment, you asked a question about the topic for a classmate to answer. 5.) You answered (replied to) at least one other student’s question at the end of their posted assignment. 6.) Your TURNITIN similarity score is 15% or LESS.

# Page 4^page=4
7.) Include in each assignment at least one quote with the page number from your text where that quote is found. The quote does not add to your minimum word count. Please page me if you would like detailed feedback on each assignment and I will provide it. Occasionally I may alter a due date for an assignment. If I do this, I will state it in the assignment posting or in the “Information” discussion area post. Otherwise, assume all due dates are as listed in the syllabus. To post an assignment, please do the following. a.) Go to the Discussions tab from the course home page. b.) Read the requirements under “Weekly Assignments”. Scroll down the page to that weeks assignment. c.) Click on the appropriate assignment posted by the instructor for that week. The text of the assignment will appear in a box at the top of the page. In the top left corner of the box at the top of the page where the assignment is listed, there will be a button labeled “Reply”. Click this button and type your answer in the box provided. d.) When you are finished typing your answer, click on “submit” in the bottom right hand of the box and your assignment will be posted in the correct spot in the correct manner automatically. Again, do NOT “attach” documents to your post. e.) Next, go to the Assignments tab and find the dropbox with the same name. Upload your assignment there. (don’t forget to check your extension (.docx, .doc, .rtf, .pdf) f.) After your file is submitted, click on “1 Submission/1File” for your Turnitin similarity score. If it is over 15%, adjust your essay until it is 15% or below. Having a submission with a score above 15% will result in it not being accepted. I will examine the post for plagiarism and if I believe it has been plagiarized, the student will IMMEDIATELY fail the course and have their name submitted to the appropriate Dean for action. If you have questions about how or when to cite correctly, please ask immediately via the pager. g.) Go back and read everyone else’s posts. Add comments to classmate’s posts by the same method (as in section c. above), using their individual posts to respond to. This will ensure that each response will be placed with the correct post. You must participate. Assignments are NOT optional. There will be one ungraded (but REQUIRED) practice assignment and twelve assignments counted throughout the semester. Failure to turn in the practice assignment means failure to complete the requirements of the course = automatic final grade reduction of one letter grade. You must turn in 7 of the 13 assignments posted for full creditduring the semester, and the practice assignment, to possibly pass this course. Any student that completes 10 of the 13 Assignments for full credit gets all the points allotted for the assignments. (200/200). Each assignment missing under the 10 full credit assignments reduces the assignment score by 75 points cumulative. (9=125, 8=50, 7=0 ) Keep in mind that assignments that do not fulfill all criteria will not count towards “full credit assignment” count. Anyone completing 6 or fewer Assignments for full credit may not pass the course. Please ask if you have any questions. Your criteria for acceptable assignments are as follows:

# Page 5^page=5
1.) minimum word length (400 words—feel free to go quite a bit over—this is a minimum, not a target) 2.) work turned in on time (late work = no points) to the Assignment tab dropbox AND Discussion section post. 3.) Good faith effort at the assignment. (If you have to ask if you put forth a good faith effort, you probably did not.) This includes the use of good grammar and the citation of source material. Always cite your sources! (See link for CMOS – Chicago manual of style) https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/chicago_manual_17th_edition/cmos_formattin g_and_style_guide/general_format.html 4.) At the end of your assignment, ask a question about the topic for a classmate to answer. 5.) You answered (replied to) at least one other student’s question at the end of their posted assignment. 6.) Your TURNITIN similarity score is 15% or LESS. 7.) Include in each assignment at least one quote with the page number from your text where that quote is found. The quote does not add to your minimum word count. Please page me if you would like detailed feedback on each assignment and I will provide it for you. Additionally, each student must receive FULL CREDIT for a minimum of 8 assignments to pass this class. This allows for someone to have up to 5 assignments without full credit and still possibly pass the class, although they would receive zero points for the assignment portion of the grade For Full credit, each student needs at least 10 full credit assignments. Full credit means that one has turned in the assignment and has fulfilled all the requirements listed in the syllabus. It is possible to turn an assignment in late, not receive full credit for it (i.e. receive points towards the total points for the course), but still have the assignment count towards the 7 assignments needed to potentially pass the class (but this would net zero points for the Assignment portion of the grade). If this is confusing to anyone, please page or call me with your questions. Since assignments are not graded in the usual manner (but are credit/no credit), I feel these are reasonable expectations for all students. No exceptions. 20% of your grade. Grading policy: There are 1000 total points for this course. All grading will be done on a straight percentage scale with 91% and above = A, 81-90 = B, 7180 = C, 61-70 = D, 60 and below = F. There is no curve. Assignments and exams may be made up only with prior consent of the instructor. Late exams are reduced 10 percentage points for each day they are late, and 10 percentage points for every 5% over 15% Turnitin similarity score. For example, an exam handed in 3 days late would be reduced 30 percent (out of a possible 100). The maximum possible points for that exam would be 70 (if one would have scored a 95 on an exam, but turned it in three days late, one would receive a 65). Points are deducted after the exam has been scored. No exceptions. Note: Always turn in your completed assignments and exams, even if they are late. Any credit is better than zero credit. Grades for exams will be returned in the “Feedback” area of the dropbox submission area. They will not be posted anyplace else. I find this works best, as it guarantees each person reads the feedback for their exam to get their grade.

# Page 6^page=6
Plagiarism and Cheating: Any student plagiarizing or cheating will immediately fail the class. The instructor will then pursue all disciplinary actions available through the college. If you use a source in your answers, ALWAYS cite the source whether it is a website or printed material (book, journal, etc.). If you have any questions about how to cite something, please ask before it becomes an issue. These issues are very serious and will be handled as such. Every assignment and exam will be checked with TURNITIN via D2L. If you have a similarity score over 15%, the student must work to lower that score to 15% or below before the due date and time for the assignment. Please Note: I may want to follow up with you about your work (i.e., ask you questions) in real time via a zoom-meeting. Should I notify you of this intent, I will work with you to arrange a zoom or in-person meeting to discuss the submission. You should be prepared to discuss in detail your study, research, and writing processes as you worked on the submission. This meeting will take place before a final grade for that exam or assignment is assigned. I intend to meet with everyone in the class at least once to discuss their work. Please see D2L class announcements for more info. Expectations: Student: I expect each student to read their assigned reading before the doing the weekly assignments. Each student should also read through at least some of the other students’ postings (about 40% would be adequate) Be prepared to discuss the material assigned for that week should the need arise, or comment on postings by other students. Turn in all assignments on or before their actual due dates. Any use of AI for writing exams or assignments, other than helping with grammar, will be considered plagiarism resulting in immediate failure for the course. Do NOT use Wikipedia, or any other wiki as a source for any of your work. You may raid the bibliography of any article published in a wiki for more information, but be sure to check out the source itself. ********Read your syllabus completely! **************************** Instructor: Exams graded in a timely manner. Confidentiality of graded material and any conferences necessary. Availability for appointments. Extra help as needed. Discussion: Occasionally I may post discussion questions in “Questions and Other Info” forum for all students to respond to throughout the week. Please respond to these at your leisure and feel free to post your own questions for your peers and myself to answer. This section will not be graded. Participation here does show effort, however, and may influence a final grade in a positive manner if the student is on the very edge of a letter grade range. Acceptable submission formats for Exams:

# Page 7^page=7
Please use Microsoft Word to submit your work. All ARCC computers have this program. Many local libraries have it as well. Acceptable formats are .pdf, .rtf,, .doc or .docx. If you do not know how to submit your exams in either of these formats, one may enter text directly into the “description” area of your dropbox submission. You will also need to submit a file to make this feature work so be sure to use the description area only as a backup if you are unsure that your submission file format is correct. Failure to submit exams in acceptable formats will be considered as if no submission had been received. All students have access to ARCC computers in the computer lab on campus. Email me a picture of your favorite animal for ten points of extra credit when you see this. It is the students’ responsibility to make sure their work is done on time and in the correct format, using the acceptable word processing programs. If you do not have MS WORD, then you may ask technology for the student version (free I think) of WORD 365 or go to www.OpenOffice.org and download their free shareware program that mimics MSWORD. File formats submitted with this program must match those of MSWORD (.docx, doc, .rtf or .pdf. The program defaults to its own format so be sure to save it in the correct format—of those formats, .rtf seems to give the least problems with posting and submission). Please see the “Questions and Other Info” section for any further information. Feel free to post questions there or page or email me at any time. I will respond as fast as possible. Pay attention to due dates, word minimums, and similarity percentages for TURNITIN. One last note: I post “Guides for the Course” guides under “Questions and Info” section under “Information: Important!” to be able to more handily navigate the course, kind of an FAQ. If you think you would like to have a guide on something you don’t see, just let me know! Thank you! Good luck and Welcome to the Class!!!!!!

Common Course Outline A. Course Prefix, Number, and Title: HIST 1103 Contemporary World History MNTC: Goal Areas 5C & 8 B. Semester Credit Value: 3 C. Prerequisites (must have a grade of C or better): None D. Recommended Skills, Abilities, or Coursework: One year of U.S. and World History in high school is recommended. E. Catalog Description: This course is a historical analysis of the contemporary world in global perspective from the aftermath of World War II to the present. Topics surveyed will include such areas as WWII and the Peace, Cold War containment, global, social and economic patterns, neo-imperialism, decolonization, peace initiatives; local and international perspectives of global conditions and events; and global terrorism. F. Course Information 1. Total classroom hours per week: 3 hours 2. Total laboratory hours per week: 0 hours 3. Total clinical hours per week: 0 hours 4. Other (rehearsals, studio, etc.) hours per week: 0 hours 5. Additional fee to student: No Ye s 6. Course is required for which of the following: A A AS A A S A FA Certificate No degree 7. Specific degree or certificate names: G. Learner Outcomes 1. Critically evaluate factual accuracy and evidentiary sources while demonstrating historical knowledge and understanding. 2. Describe and discuss the sociopolitical and socioeconomic aspects of various states in the contemporary era, demonstrating historical knowledge and understanding from informed perspectives and demonstrating appropriate appreciation and tolerance of diversity. 3. Analyze a variety of global problems, patterns, events, people, and themes with an eye to developing workable solutions for contemporary problems and enabling students to become active participants in democracy at local, state, national, and global levels. 4. Participate actively in discussions on core contemporary World History issues-problems, peoples, historic forces, patterns of global interdependence, contemporary political, economic, and social issues, and problems of cross-cultural differences that block real understanding. 5. Demonstrate historical knowledge and understanding about what concepts of world peace and world citizenship mean and how they are of foundational importance for the United Nations.
